harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Created Fleet Internal CA, installed it as a system trust anchor on both nodes, issued node2 a CA-signed certificate, and configured persistent HTTPS on TCP/8443. Both nodes retained RHEL 10.0 and kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0.x86_64. Sequential restart testing confirmed persistence and recovery.
actions_performed: Installed compatible OpenSSL tooling without changing the OS release or kernel.
Created a 3072-bit RSA CA named Fleet Internal CA on node1.
Generated node2's private key and CSR on node2, including DNS:node2 and IP:10.100.196.11 SANs.
Signed node2's TLS server certificate on node1 and installed it on node2.
Installed the CA into both RHEL system trust stores.
Configured and enabled fleet-https.service on node2, listening on TCP/8443.
Persistently allowed TCP/8443 through node2's firewalld configuration.
Verified trusted HTTPS locally and remotely without bypassing certificate validation.
Restarted node1 and node2 sequentially, proving changed boot identities and full recovery after each restart.

evidence.requirement: Create Fleet Internal CA and trust it on node1
evidence.summary: CA subject and issuer are CN=Fleet Internal CA; node1's default system trust verifies the issued node2 certificate.

evidence.requirement: Issue a valid TLS certificate for node2
evidence.summary: The CSR and installed certificate contain DNS:node2 and IP:10.100.196.11; issuer is Fleet Internal CA and server-auth verification succeeds.

evidence.requirement: Install the CA as a trusted system authority on node2
evidence.summary: node2's installed anchor matches node1's CA fingerprint, and default system verification returns OK before and after restart.

evidence.requirement: Serve trusted HTTPS on node2 port 8443
evidence.summary: The service is active and enabled, firewalld permits TCP/8443, TLS hostname verification returns code 0, and both nodes receive the expected HTTPS content.

evidence.requirement: Preserve installed operating-system release and kernel
evidence.summary: Both nodes reported RHEL 10.0 and kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0.x86_64 before changes and after restart testing.
Healthy baseline boot ID 646e5f74-dc0e-45e7-9746-226c4351af28; reboot acknowledged; recovered boot ID cb6b5b3f-7ba6-4c1e-8034-4b7f4c2ced75; CA material, trust, TLS, and HTTPS remained healthy.

Healthy baseline boot ID 03408ac4-bfe4-4151-98bd-1966b0a205af; reboot acknowledged and connection closed during restart; recovered boot ID c55f762d-e040-4cc6-8278-19e887c828bb; service, listener, firewall, certificate, trust, and HTTPS content recovered locally and remotely.
